clue.text: Being shelled, company ultimately surrendered, utterly beaten

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter of the word before it, the one that gets given up
something surrendered is handed over and lost, so a letter leaves the fodder
beaten as in whisked, as eggs are, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the last letter of company, taken away
the anagram fodder, before losing a letter

explanation.surface: A company under shellfire gives in, thoroughly defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: UTTERLY loses its Y, and UTTERL is rearranged into TURTLE. The surface is military shelling; the definition is a creature that lives inside a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A turtle is a reptile protected by a hard carapace, so it is a creature literally encased in shell.

clue.text: Charity event on the tiles is cancelled unfortunately

indicators.note: cancelled means struck out, so the word is is removed from the fodder
something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the remaining letters are disordered

blocks.note: the phrase taken letter for letter as fodder
the two letters that are cancelled

explanation.surface: A night out on the tiles has been called off, much to everyone's regret.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking IS out of ONTHETILES leaves ONTHETLE, which rearranges to the answer. 'On the tiles' is British slang for a night of carousing.
explanation.definitionFit: A telethon is a long televised broadcast raising money for good causes, a fundraising occasion.

clue.text: Paper finished with further edits

blocks.note: a ream is a standard quantity of paper, 500 sheets
finished means came to a close

explanation.surface: A newspaper has been completed with yet more revisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reamended has been amended again, that is, corrected or revised a second time.

clue.text: Male variant of chromosome or female?

blocks.note: a lad is a boy or young man
the Y chromosome is one of the two kinds of sex chromosome

explanation.surface: A biology question: is the Y chromosome the male variant, or the female one?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Male variant of chromosome' as one phrase, but Male is a separate piece. Ladies dancing belong to The Twelve Days of Christmas, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a woman, so the word stands for a female person; the question mark admits the noun-for-adjective looseness.

clue.text: Reckoning opener's out, preparing to bat

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, and being out it is dropped from the phrase

blocks.note: a cricketer pads up, straps on leg pads, before going in to bat

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: the opening batsman is out, and the next one is getting ready.
explanation.walkthrough: PADDING UP loses its first letter. In cricket an opener is a batsman who starts the innings, which makes 'opener's out' look like match commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding up figures is totting them up, which is calculating or computing a total.

clue.text: One beating master in gruesome murder

indicators.note: gruesome suggests a body left mangled, so these letters are mangled into another order
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: M is a standard abbreviation for master
the letters rearranged around the inserted letter

explanation.surface: A crime story: someone thrashing their boss in a grisly killing.
explanation.walkthrough: MURDER rearranges to DRUMER and takes M inside. Drummers drumming are one of The Twelve Days of Christmas gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer is a percussionist who strikes, or beats, a drum.

clue.text: Identifier of books switching focus, collecting European playwright

indicators.note: switching the letters at the centre of the word swaps their order
collecting means gathering in, so one piece takes another inside it

blocks.note: the International Standard Book Number printed on every book
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A cataloguing code is changed in emphasis and picks up a European entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters of ISBN swap places to give IBSN, and E goes in before the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: They're a-laying Easter eggs, oddly from the bottom

indicators.note: oddly means take the letters in the odd-numbered positions only
in a down entry, reading from the bottom means reading upwards, the wrong way round

blocks.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Hens busy producing Easter eggs, laid in an odd fashion from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of Easter eggs are read upwards. 'A-laying' quotes the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas: six geese a-laying.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese are the birds in the carol's line about six of them laying eggs, so they are the ones a-laying.

clue.text: Scottish drone operators?

blocks.note: surface reading: people in Scotland flying unmanned aircraft
setter's reading: the drone is the pipe of a bagpipe sounding one continuous note, played by Highland musicians

explanation.walkthrough: A drone today suggests a remote-controlled aircraft, but the bagpipe's bass pipes are also drones. Pipers piping are another gift from the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipe players work an instrument whose drones hum under the melody, and the bagpipe is Scotland's emblematic instrument.

clue.text: University's invested in property attracting American capital

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within another
attracting means drawing something along, so a further piece is attached

blocks.note: land is real estate, property
U is the usual abbreviation for university
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A university has put money into real estate and drawn American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money in this financial surface, but it is the definition, a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Luanda is the capital city of Angola, on the Atlantic coast of southern Africa.

clue.text: Snooze more than refreshed upset Leo

indicators.note: refreshed means made anew, so the letters are rebuilt in fresh order

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone tries to out-nap a lion-starred friend who is grumpy after resting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; refreshed does the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsleep someone is to sleep longer than them, to keep dozing after they wake.

clue.text: Ruler being lengthened at either end

blocks.clueFragment: Ruler being lengthened at either end
blocks.note: surface reading: a measuring rule being extended at both ends
setter's reading: a nobleman or sovereign, whose title grows at both ends in the carol's line about ten of them leaping

explanation.walkthrough: The ruler looks like a measuring stick, but it is a nobleman. The wordplay is unclear: the outer letters of lengthened frame the word, with OR in the middle unaccounted for.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord is a nobleman or feudal master holding power over others, a sovereign or governor.

clue.text: Greek goddess rejecting wings immediately

indicators.note: the wings are the two outermost letters, and rejecting them throws both away

blocks.note: Athene, also Athena, Greek goddess of wisdom

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess spurns her wings at once.
explanation.walkthrough: ATHENE loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Then can mean straight after that, next in time, close to the sense of promptly following.

clue.text: When podcasting, usual browser is appropriate

indicators.note: a podcast is heard rather than read, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: a deer browses on shoots and leaves, and a usual one is common

explanation.surface: A tech tip: the default web browser is fine to use while making a podcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' is not software but a grazing animal. 'Appropriate' is the verb, to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer is to seize property for one's own use, which is what appropriate means as a verb.

clue.text: Without 4 iron making longest par on course

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A golfer without the four-iron tackles the course's longest hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all golf, where a 4 iron is a club; here 4 is a Roman numeral and iron its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf holes are par three, four or five, so a par five is the longest kind on a standard course.

clue.text: Passenger pigeon or dodo? Certainly no spring chicken!

blocks.note: first meaning: an avian species long gone, extinct for centuries
second meaning: a slangy phrase for an older woman or person

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves sound like birds, but the second is the idiom for someone no longer young. 'Bird' is British slang for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct species are ancient avian types, and 'no spring chicken' describes someone well past youth, a familiar idiom.

clue.text: Prolific poster heartlessly lying about plans again

indicators.note: without a heart, the central letter is cut out
about means turned round, so the letters are read the other way

blocks.note: a spammer sends out masses of unwanted messages

explanation.surface: A cynical picture of a relentless online poster who lies without a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAMMER loses its middle M to give SPAMER, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To remap is to chart or lay out again, so remaps fits the verb plans again.

clue.text: Dresser from Kentish Town discounted by nearly fifteen pounds

indicators.note: discounted means reduced, so a chunk of letters is taken off

blocks.note: Maidstone is the county town of Kent
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds, one short of fifteen

explanation.surface: A sideboard from a London district is marked down by almost fifteen quid.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a real London district, which hides the Kent town in the wordplay. 'Pounds' suggests money but means weight. Maids a-milking are carol gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's maid helps her mistress dress, so she is a dresser in the sense of an attendant.

clue.text: Game character atop Crib Goch?

indicators.note: atop means sitting above, and in a down entry the higher piece comes first

blocks.note: a part is a character or role played by an actor
Crib Goch is a famous knife-edge mountain crest in Snowdonia, Wales

explanation.surface: A video-game character standing on top of a Welsh mountain crest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game character' reads as one phrase, but Game is the definition, meaning birds shot for sport. The partridge in a pear tree opens the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: A partridge is a plump bird shot for sport, and game is the collective term for such quarry.

clue.text: Cuckoo ensnared as source of paté

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go haywire into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A cuckoo is trapped and ends up in paté.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like the bird caught in a trap; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté ardennais is a coarse pork pâté named after the Ardennes, the forested region where it originates.

clue.text: Daughter hiding inside to avoid notice

indicators.note: something hiding inside is tucked within another piece

blocks.note: to avert is to ward off or avoid
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter hides indoors so nobody spots her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' reads as attention in the surface, but it is a noun meaning a public announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a printed or broadcast announcement, a notice in the sense of a published advertisement.

clue.text: Dressing easy as ABC to nurses

indicators.note: easy suggests loose and relaxed, so the letters are freed to rearrange
to nurse is to hold close, so one piece cradles the other

blocks.note: taken as written, the outer piece
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Applying a wound dressing is as easy as ABC for nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a nurse bandaging a wound; dressing is a sauce for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a fiery chilli sauce used as a condiment, the culinary kind of dressing.

clue.text: Troublemaker out of prison finally for impeccable behaviour

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: stir is slang for prison
last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is released early from jail for good conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of prison' sounds like release, but 'out of' just means made from.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrer is someone who deliberately causes discord or mischief among others.

clue.text: Where dam's found scrubbing a pen?

indicators.note: scrubbing something means cancelling it, so a letter is struck off

blocks.note: the Aswan High Dam crosses the Nile in Egypt
the letter removed

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where a mother animal lives, minus a writing pen.
explanation.walkthrough: A dam is also a mother animal and a pen a writing tool, but here pen is a female of the answer bird, hence the question mark. Swans a-swimming are carol gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is the female of the swan, so pen is an example of the bird, flagged by the question mark.

clue.text: Ditch foxtrot for tango from Paris, perhaps

indicators.note: one thing for another means swapping it in its place

blocks.note: a trench is a ditch
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancer from Paris drops the foxtrot for the tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a verb meaning drop; it is the noun. French hens are the third gift in the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Parisians are French, and the question mark marks Paris as one example of the nationality's places.

clue.text: Rugby forward caught naked in daily strip

indicators.note: caught as in heard, so the next word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
forward in the sense of cheeky or bold
naked means uncovered

explanation.surface: A rugby forward is snapped unclothed in a newspaper, or stripping on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' is a rugby position in the surface but an adjective here. The answer is a cartoon bear in checked trousers, running in the Daily Express since 1920.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Bear is a long-running children's comic strip printed in a British newspaper every day.

clue.text: Small gem lettuce's beginning to bear fruit

indicators.note: beginning points to the opening letter of the word it is attached to
to bear is to carry, so one piece carries the other along at its tail

blocks.note: a pear is a fruit
the beginning of lettuce

explanation.surface: A Little Gem lettuce is starting to produce fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small gem' looks like the lettuce variety Little Gem, but it is the definition. The pear tree is from the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a small lustrous bead from an oyster, prized as a precious jewel.

clue.text: New charging equipment introducing special tolls

indicators.note: charging means rushing in, so a letter drives into another piece
introducing means bringing in next, so a further piece follows

blocks.note: a rig is a set of equipment
N is the standard abbreviation for new
S is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A new electric-car charger brings in special road charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tolls' looks like road fees, but it is the verb for bells. Gold rings are the carol's fifth gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell tolls when it sounds slowly, and rings is the general verb for a bell sounding.

clue.text: Cadet wanting adult in plane?

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the following letters are left out

blocks.note: a cadet is a trainee in the services
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'In plane' looks like a flight, but 'in' belongs to the letters removed and plane is the tree. The pear tree completes the carol's first line.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a broad-leaved tree common in London streets, so it is one example of the answer.

clue.text: One might want to settle in Andover

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the place name that follows

blocks.note: the middle four letters

explanation.definitionFit: A dove is a political moderate who seeks peace, so it is someone keen to resolve a conflict.

clue.text: Dine with head following name order

blocks.note: N is an abbreviation for name

a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests the top of the table but is a headland, a ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness is tidiness, the state of things arranged in good order.

clue.text: Turn 50 with day at space fair

blocks.note: a go is a turn in a game
fifty in Roman numerals

an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn 50' looks like reaching an age; turn and 50 are separate pieces. An en is a typesetter's space half an em wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden describes blond hair, and fair also means light-haired, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Hard base pilot's exploited as landing pad

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
e is the base of natural logarithms
the six letters rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard base' reads as a fortified site, but it splits into two single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A helistop is a small helipad where helicopters set down, a place for touching down.

clue.text: Note saints when checking church alcove

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
CE is the Church of England
SS is the abbreviation for saints

explanation.walkthrough: 'Checking' suggests inspecting the church; here it means restraining, the outer pair holding the church abbreviation in.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a niche set back into a wall, the same thing as an alcove.
